plain.text: Later, Jesus appeared to his disciples by the Sea of Galilee. Peter and six others went fishing, but caught nothing all night. At dawn Jesus stood on the shore, though they did not recognise him. He told them to throw their net on the right side of the boat. They caught so many fish they could not haul the net in. The disciple whom Jesus loved said, "It is the Lord!" Peter jumped into the water. On shore was a fire with fish and bread. Jesus said, "Come and have breakfast." There were 153 large fish, yet the net did not tear. This was the third time Jesus appeared to his disciples after he was raised.

After breakfast, Jesus asked Simon Peter, "Do you love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." "Feed my lambs." He asked a second time, and said, "Take care of my sheep." The third time Peter was hurt and said, "Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my sheep." He told Peter that when he was old, others would lead him where he did not want to go, showing the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God. Then he said, "Follow me!"

Peter saw the disciple whom Jesus loved and asked, "Lord, what about him?" Jesus said, "If I want him to remain alive until I return, what is that to you? You must follow me." So a rumour spread that this disciple would not die, but Jesus had not said that. This is the disciple who testifies to these things and wrote them down. Jesus did many other things; if every one were written down, the whole world could not contain the books.

summary.bigIdea: The risen Jesus restores Peter after his denials and calls him again: "Follow me."
points: Jesus provides a huge catch of fish and cooks breakfast for his friends.
Three times Jesus asks Peter, "Do you love me?", and gives him work to do.
Jesus tells Peter not to compare himself with others, but to follow him.
summary.reflection: Peter had failed badly, yet Jesus gave him a fresh start. Where would you like a fresh start?
